name: Geir Engdahl
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, AI, Cognite (Oslo)
profile: Norwegian technologist who co-founded industrial-data/AI software company Cognite in 2016 with John Markus Lervik and others. Previously founded ML classifieds startup Snapsale (acquired by Schibsted in 2017) and was a senior software engineer at Google. Served as Cognite CTO, then Chief Product Officer (2024), and was named CTO, AI in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Before Cognite he founded Snapsale (2011), a machine-learning classifieds startup he ran as CEO/CTO until Schibsted acquired it in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He won a silver medal at the International Olympiad in Informatics, and holds a master's in computational science from the University of Oslo.
notes: Press contact is Cognite's VP Global PR (Michelle Holford) as listed in 2024 release; may have changed. Role update: https://itbrief.co.uk/story/cognite-appoints-ai-leaders-to-drive-innovation-push

name: Matias Muchnick
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, NotCo (The Not Company)
profile: Chilean entrepreneur who co-founded NotCo in 2015 with Karim Pichara and Pablo Zamora, using its AI 'Giuseppe' to formulate plant-based foods (NotMilk, NotMayo); backed by Jeff Bezos' fund and valued at ~$1.5B+. In 2025-26 NotCo pivoted toward selling its AI formulation platform to food majors (Kraft Heinz JV, Ferrero, Coca-Cola), exiting several consumer markets.
interesting_fact: Named to TIME's Next Generation Leaders; NotCo attracted investors including Bezos Expeditions and Roger Federer.
deep_cut_fact: Before NotCo he left finance to launch Eggless, a vegan mayonnaise brand in Chile; earlier still his first startup, a gamified-wellness app called Chooz, was in his words 'a total failure'.
notes: Active on LinkedIn and frequent podcast guest. No published press email found in quick search; go via NotCo comms (notco.com).

name: Francisco Padilla
current_role: Co-founder of Konfío (Mexico City SME lender); described as growth director / formerly CTO
profile: Mexican technologist who co-founded Konfío in 2013 with David Arana, building its AI-driven self-service SME credit platform; Konfío became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1.3B valuation) and has since obtained a banking licence. Padilla has held CTO/CIO and growth-director titles; Arana is CEO.
interesting_fact: Konfío's very first loan, for 10,000 pesos, was made in January 2014; by 2024-25 the company was disbursing more than 17 billion pesos and had backed ~80,000 businesses.
deep_cut_fact: A 2007 Tec de Monterrey computer-technologies grad, he met co-founder David Arana while both worked at MicroStrategy in New York (Citibank was its biggest client) during the 2008 crisis; his parents, both systems engineers, advised him not to quit.
notes: Low public profile compared with CEO David Arana; current exact title unclear (El CEO interview calls him cofundador y director de crecimiento: https://elceo.com/negocios/konfio-del-unicornio-fintech-al-reto-de-convertirse-en-banco/). Best route via Konfío corporate comms.

name: Sean Hendelman
current_role: CEO, Active Trading division, Clear Street (since May 2024); co-founder and board member, Public.com
profile: New York trading entrepreneur who founded T3 (T3 Live, T3 Trading Group), a trading, training and technology provider for professional traders, and co-founded social investing app Public.com, where he sits on the board. In 2024 prime broker Clear Street hired him to run its active trading division.
interesting_fact: Spent most of a 25+ year career running T3, building a global platform spanning equities, options, futures and algorithmic trading, before co-founding retail investing app Public.com.
notes: Clear Street bio: https://www.clearstreet.io/about/team/sean-hendelman (page errored on fetch). No published personal contact found; route via Clear Street media relations.

name: Kabir Shahani
current_role: Founder, Amp It Up Ventures; co-founder and former CEO of Amperity; Affiliate Assistant Professor, UW Information School
profile: Seattle entrepreneur (b. 1982, Kansas City) who co-founded health-marketing software firm Appature (sold to IMS Health in 2013) and then customer-data platform Amperity (2016) with Derek Slager, leading it to unicorn status before stepping down as CEO in 2022. He now incubates and backs software startups through Amp It Up Ventures and teaches at UW.
interesting_fact: Holds more than 10 US patents spanning databases, entity resolution and machine learning; Amperity worked with UW's Dan Suciu on a probabilistic customer database.
deep_cut_fact: He founded his first company at 24 and was named the U.S. Small Business Administration's Young Entrepreneur of the Year in 2012; he earned a BS in Informatics from UW in 2004.
notes: Email is his UW iSchool affiliate-faculty address published by the university. 2024 GeekWire piece on his new venture: https://www.geekwire.com/2024/ex-amperity-ceo-kabir-shahani-is-amped-about-building-startups-with-his-latest-venture/

name: Chris Hood
current_role: Co-founder, Go1 (Brisbane-born workplace learning platform)
profile: Australian software engineer and one of Go1's four co-founders (with Andrew Barnes, Vu Tran and Chris Eigeland). Go1 grew from a Logan/Brisbane garage web-dev business into a corporate e-learning content aggregator valued at about $2B, Brisbane's first unicorn. Hood is the technical co-founder who built the platform's software.
interesting_fact: Go1 began as a web development business started in a garage by school friends; it became Brisbane's first tech unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Andrew Barnes met Hood at a tech conference; in Go1's early days, when salespeople promised features that didn't exist yet, Hood had to build them fast - 'It's how we learnt what people wanted.'
notes: Very low public profile; current title not confirmed. Griffith University alumnus and ex-Intellidesign software engineer per Crunchbase (unverified). Route via Go1 (go1.com/about-us).

name: Chris Suarez
current_role: Co-founder, PLACE, Inc. (real estate team platform); leads Xperience Brokerage Network and Xperience Growth Coaching
profile: Portland-area real estate entrepreneur who founded Xperience, a top Keller Williams expansion organisation, then in 2020 co-founded PLACE with Ben Kinney, a platform providing tech, back-office and services to top agent teams across 100+ US/Canada markets; PLACE reached unicorn valuation. He also owns brokerage offices and runs coaching/mastermind programmes.
interesting_fact: PLACE launched in early 2020 already carrying $1.5B in sales and $40M revenue from its founders' existing businesses, just as COVID-19 hit.
deep_cut_fact: He and Ben Kinney shared the 2023 EY Entrepreneur Of The Year Mountain West Award; he hosts the podcast 'Xperience Growth with Chris Suarez'.

public_contacts.value: Xperience Growth with Chris Suarez (Apple Podcasts)

notes: Active speaker/coach with his own site and podcast - accessible. Team page: https://place.com/team/

name: Bao Chunjian
current_role: Founder and CEO, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通), Shenzhen
profile: Chinese engineer (USTC computer science graduate) who spent ~9 years at Tencent, rising to data-centre director in its data platform department, before founding Xiaoe-tech, a SaaS platform that lets creators, educators and brands sell paid knowledge content, courses and live streams. Tencent is a major shareholder (~16.8%); the company has been preparing a Hong Kong listing.
interesting_fact: At Tencent he reached the rare 'T4 expert engineer' technical rank before leaving in 2015 to start his own business.
deep_cut_fact: Xiaoe-tech's prototype was a one-month rebuild of the paid-audio and membership system for finance writer Wu Xiaobo's 'Wu Xiaobo Channel' in 2016; Wu then invested. His first venture, a blue-collar hiring app called 工作帮, shut after about seven months.
notes: Known internally as 'Lao Bao'; hosts Xiaoe-tech's live interview series 老鲍对话标杆客户. Chinese-language outreach via Xiaoe-tech (xiaoe-tech.com) recommended. Education details vary across sources.

name: Raj De Datta
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Bloomreach (Mountain View, CA)
profile: Princeton engineer and Harvard MBA who co-founded Bloomreach with Ashutosh Garg in 2009; the AI-driven digital commerce platform (search, personalisation, marketing automation) says it powers brands representing ~25% of US and UK retail e-commerce. Earlier he was an EIR at Mohr Davidow, a Cisco product-marketing director and a Lazard tech banker; he is also a Founder Partner at Founder Collective.
interesting_fact: He is author of the bestselling book 'The Digital Seeker', a playbook for digital teams, and has backed 20+ startups as an individual investor.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the US Tennis Association's Council for Player Development and on the board of RepresentUs, a bipartisan democracy-reform group; early in his career he was a founding team member of telecom startup FirstMark Communications.
notes: Writes bylined columns (CMSWire, Total Retail) and does podcasts - receptive to thought-leadership outreach. Route via Bloomreach comms.

name: Michel Tricot
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Airbyte (San Francisco)
profile: French data engineer who co-founded open-source data-integration company Airbyte in 2020 with John Lafleur (YC W20); Airbyte's connector platform became one of the most widely used ELT tools and was valued around $1.5B in 2021. Before that he was Head of Integrations/Director of Engineering at LiveRamp and a founding engineering leader at rideOS (later acquired by Gopuff).
interesting_fact: At LiveRamp he spent about seven years building and scaling more than 1,000 data connectors - the pain point that inspired Airbyte's open-source connector model.
deep_cut_fact: His data career began around 2008 as an R&D engineer handling financial data at FactSet in Paris; on YC's profile he says he has 'been working in data since 2007'.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Airflow Summit, Percona Live, RAISE). Also a venture partner at Flex Capital (per profiles, unverified). Route via Airbyte.

name: Ricardo Salgado
current_role: Co-founder of Loadsmart; reportedly Executive Chairman since May 2022 (Felipe Capella is CEO)
profile: Georgia Tech-trained engineer and former Goldman Sachs investor (New York, London, Brazil) who co-founded New York-based freight-tech company Loadsmart with Felipe Capella in 2014. Loadsmart automates full-truckload brokerage with instant pricing and booking via API and reached unicorn status in 2022. Salgado led as CEO until Capella took over in May 2022.
interesting_fact: Loadsmart claimed the first nationwide instant pricing and booking for full-truckload shipments and the first enterprise API of its kind; about 45% of its early team were engineers and data scientists.
deep_cut_fact: Before freight, he spent years at Goldman Sachs, including helping set up a capital-structure investing team in Brazil covering Latin American credit and equities - where he first saw how fragmented freight brokerage was.
notes: Current title not confirmed by a primary Loadsmart source. FreightWaves speaker page: https://live.freightwaves.com/event-speakers/ricardo-salgado. Route via Loadsmart.

name: Zhang Jihui (Jeffrey Tiong)
current_role: Founder and CEO, PatSnap (Singapore/Beijing)
profile: 'Zhang Jihui' appears to be the Mandarin rendering of Jeffrey Tiong Jee Hui, NUS bioengineering graduate who founded PatSnap in 2007 with Dian Guan. PatSnap is an AI-driven patent and R&D intelligence platform (Eureka, Analytics) serving 10,000+ customers, valued above $1B after a 2021 SoftBank Vision Fund 2-led round.
interesting_fact: PatSnap started in Singapore with a SGD 50,000 grant from NUS Enterprise; Vertex Ventures was its first investor.
deep_cut_fact: The idea came from an internship at a medical-device startup in Philadelphia (via NUS Overseas College), where his supervisor asked him to research patents - his first encounter with IP search.
notes: Name match inferred: Tiong = Zhang (张) in Hokkien and 'Jee Hui' = Jihui; MarketScreener lists 'Jeffrey Jee Hui Tiong'. Confirm before outreach. Route via PatSnap comms.

name: Rajoshi Ghosh
current_role: Co-founder of Hasura; listed as Co-founder & Chief Ecosystem Officer at PromptQL (Hasura's AI spin-out/rebrand)
profile: Co-founded Hasura with Tanmai Gopal; its open-source GraphQL engine let developers spin up real-time APIs on databases and passed 100M+ downloads, with the company valued at $1B in 2022. She served as COO, and the founders have since launched PromptQL, an AI data-agent platform. She studied computational biology at NUS (per profiles).
interesting_fact: Hasura's open-source GraphQL engine reached more than 100 million downloads within about two years of launch.
deep_cut_fact: Hasura began as her idea for a healthy home-cooked food delivery company in Chennai; the founders pivoted when local developers wanted to use Tanmai's backend platform 'procrust.es', which evolved into Hasura - and she admits they were reluctant to drop the food idea.
notes: Current PromptQL title from a conference speaker page (https://www.ai-infra-summit.com/speakers/rajoshi-ghosh); verify. Route via Hasura/PromptQL.

name: Laura Behrens Wu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Shippo (San Francisco)
profile: German-born entrepreneur who left her University of St. Gallen master's to co-found Shippo in San Francisco (2013-14) with Simon Kreuz; the multi-carrier shipping API/platform serves 100,000+ e-commerce merchants and was valued at $1B in 2021. In 2026 she is still CEO, pushing AI-driven shipping analytics ('Shippo Intelligence').
interesting_fact: Shippo was born after she and Simon Kreuz ran an online shop as students and found shipping was the problem they couldn't solve; she was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 and Inc.'s Female Founders 100.
deep_cut_fact: She came to the US for a compulsory master's internship intending to stay just three months ('Ich hatte die Absicht, nur drei Monate zu bleiben'); she was named HSG (St. Gallen) Founder of the Year in 2015.
notes: Media contact listed on Shippo's Oct 2026 press release. Speaks German; featured in the German government's 'Makers of Tomorrow' series.

name: Sidney Zhang
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Magic Eden (multi-chain NFT/crypto marketplace)
profile: Georgia Tech computer-science master's graduate and former Uber and Facebook engineering manager (AI/ML, search and recommendations) who co-founded Magic Eden in 2021 with Jack Lu, Zhuoxun Yin and Zhuojie Zhou. Magic Eden became the leading Solana NFT marketplace, expanded to Bitcoin Ordinals and other chains, hit a $1.6B valuation in 2022 and launched its ME token in Dec 2024.
interesting_fact: Magic Eden reached unicorn status within about nine months of launch in 2021-22.
deep_cut_fact: He was among the first engineers on the team at Uber in 2015 tasked with figuring out how the ride-share company could deliver food - what became Uber Eats; he later worked on Uber's self-driving unit. He met co-founder Zhuojie Zhou at Uber.
notes: Current title confirmed only via secondary sources listing Magic Eden's about page; no 2025-26 role news found. Earlier co-founded blockchain dev platform HelloBlock (https://cryptoslate.com/why-this-top-cto-ditched-uber-facebook-for-nfts-on-solana/).

name: Mickey Bresman
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Semperis (Hoboken, NJ)
profile: Israeli-born cybersecurity entrepreneur who co-founded Semperis (with Guy Teverovsky and Matan Liberman) to protect and recover Microsoft Active Directory/Entra ID identity systems from cyberattacks; he moved from Israel to New York in 2015 to build US operations, and the company passed a $1B valuation in 2022. Earlier he was CTO of YouCC Technologies, a Microsoft Gold Partner integrator.
interesting_fact: Semperis focuses on identity resilience - recovering Active Directory after ransomware, a niche many companies only discover when their identity system goes down.
deep_cut_fact: He began his technical career in the Israeli Navy's computing unit, and holds a B.A. in Technical Management with a minor in Electronic Engineering.

public_contacts.value: Semperis 'Contact Us' form linked from his official bio page

notes: Regular contributor to SC Media and speaker at RSA Conference. Calcalist profile on Israel-NY move: https://www.calcalistech.com/ctech/articles/0,7340,L-3891496,00.html

name: Jeff Jurinak
current_role: Co-founder of KoBold Metals (formerly COO); current involvement unclear - no longer on KoBold's team page
profile: Petroleum engineer with a 30+ year exploration-and-production career, largely at Conoco/ConocoPhillips, who co-founded AI-driven mineral-exploration company KoBold Metals in 2018 with Kurt House and Josh Goldman. KoBold, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Andreessen Horowitz, hunts lithium, copper, nickel and cobalt for batteries and made a major copper discovery in Zambia.
interesting_fact: KoBold applies machine learning and data science to find battery metals; its founders first worked together in 2014 at Phase Change Resources, building a data-science-driven oil and gas acquisition platform.
notes: Alive status not explicitly confirmed (no reports of death found). KoBold's about page still names him as a founder but gives no bio; Crunchbase shows COO, other profiles say former COO. Very low public profile - consider featuring Kurt House instead.

name: Shrini Viswanath
current_role: Co-founder, Upstox (RKSV Securities), Mumbai; former CTO, now in a strategic role
profile: Co-founded RKSV Securities in 2009 with Ravi Kumar and Raghu Kumar; it moved into flat-fee online retail broking in 2012 and launched the Upstox trading platform in 2016. Upstox, backed by Tiger Global, grew into one of India's largest discount brokers with 10M+ users and a ~$3.5B valuation (2021). Viswanath led technology until an external CTO was hired in 2021.
interesting_fact: More than 80% of Upstox's new customers come from India's tier 2 and tier 3 cities, per Viswanath.
deep_cut_fact: RKSV was set up in 2009 purely as a proprietary trading firm; only in 2012 did it pivot to retail broking with an online-only, flat-fee unlimited trading plan.
notes: Lower profile than CEO Ravi Kumar. Undergraduate degree from University of Illinois per MarketScreener (aggregator, unverified). Route via Upstox corporate comms.

name: Borya Shakhnovich
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of airSlate (stepped down as President & CEO in July 2025); current role not publicly announced
profile: Scientist-turned-software-entrepreneur with a computational biophysics/bioinformatics background who led pdfFiller as CEO from 2012 and built it into airSlate (2018), a Boston-based document-workflow company (pdfFiller, signNow, DocHub, US Legal Forms) valued at $1.25B in 2021. Co-founder Vadim Yasinovsky took over as CEO on 7 July 2025.
interesting_fact: airSlate, founded by Ukrainian-born entrepreneurs with large engineering teams in Ukraine, became a unicorn in 2021 after a $51M round led by G Squared and General Catalyst.
deep_cut_fact: Before software he was an academic: a post-doctoral fellow at Harvard and an assistant professor at Boston University working in computational biophysics.
notes: Left airSlate CEO role July 2025 (https://scroll.media/en/?p=19638); no new venture found. Avoid referencing the departure in outreach.

name: Arvin Vohra
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Redaptive (San Francisco), energy-as-a-service provider
profile: Former Barclays Capital power-and-utilities banker who co-founded Redaptive with John Rhow in 2014. Redaptive funds and installs LED, HVAC, solar and metering upgrades for large building portfolios at no upfront cost, paid back from savings, and uses its Redaptive ONE data platform to verify results; it raised a $250M round and reached unicorn status - squarely in the energy/data space.
interesting_fact: Redaptive ran an LED and HVAC retrofit across 430 Iron Mountain facilities in five countries at no upfront cost to Iron Mountain.
deep_cut_fact: Before Redaptive he was VP of Project Finance at lighting-controls firm Enlighted, where he created and ran its Lighting-as-a-Service (GEO) platform, and at Barclays he worked on the PACE (Property Assessed Clean Energy) program.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast - energy-as-a-service and building-energy data. Gives interviews readily (Pulse 2.0, 2025). Route via Redaptive (redaptive.com).
